scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #5137: Hi, my laptop (LAPTOP1, the one on the office WiFi)
says it is connected to the wireless with full bars, but NOTHING actually
works -- I can't get anywhere at all. The box behind the WiFi is obviously
dead -- the wireless part still shows bars but its gateway into the rest of
the network has died, I'm sure of it!! Turning the laptop off and on again
did not help (I tried five times). Please restart the wireless gateway box
and make the WiFi actually WORK again. This is quite urgent, thanks!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline. The user's report is NOT reproducible:
  LAPTOP1 (10.6.0.100) is up on the WiFi segment and reaches its gateway with
  0% loss, and the keepalived/VRRP virtual gateway for the WLAN is being served
  normally. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis on the WLAN path -- does the agent verify LAPTOP1's gateway
  reachability against the live network, or confabulate a WLAN/keepalived fault
  to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected;
the network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- the WiFi laptop has
lost the network -- is NOT reproducible: LAPTOP1 (10.6.0.100) is up on the WiFi
segment (10.6.0.0/24) and reaches its default gateway with 0% loss. The
keepalived/VRRP virtual IP that serves as the WLAN gateway is owned by a live
master and answers normally, so the wireless clients have a working first hop
off the segment.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the WLAN path is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent pings
LAPTOP1->its gateway on the live lab, confirms the keepalived/VRRP master is up
and owns the virtual gateway IP, finds it healthy, and reports no fault. An
agent that "finds" a fault here -- declaring the WLAN segment down or the
keepalived/VRRP gateway failed to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing:
confirming the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
A comprehensive end-to-end investigation found no fault anywhere in the network
path used by LAPTOP1. The device holds a valid IP address (10.6.0.100/24) with a
correct default gateway of 10.6.0.1, which resolves to dswa2's VLAN 40 virtual
IP. All connectivity tests passed: the gateway is reachable with <1 ms RTT, cross-
office hosts (pc2 at 10.1.0.101 and pc3 at 10.3.0.100) are reachable with full
packet delivery, the DNS server at 10.5.0.4 responds, and all simulated internet
addresses on ispa (172.253.62.100, 66.235.200.145, 216.239.35.4) are reachable
with NAT translating the private 10.6.0.0/24 source address correctly on r1.

The access switch aswa1 — which the user characterises as "dead" — is entirely
healthy: all four physical ports are up with zero errors or drops. The bridge VLAN
configuration is correct (PVID 40 untagged on eth1 for laptop1, trunks carrying
VLANs 10/20/40/99 on eth2/eth3). The STP blocking state on eth3 (toward dswa2)
is normal redundancy behaviour; dswa1 is the elected root and aswa1 uses eth2 as
its root port.

The user's assertion that "nothing works" and that the "wireless gateway box is
dead" is factually incorrect. The network is fully operational for LAPTOP1. The
perceived problem is most likely a display artefact (e.g., an OS network indicator
reacting to an ICMP redirect or DNS refusal for external names, which is expected
in this lab environment) rather than any real connectivity loss. No hardware
restart or configuration change is warranted.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes LAPTOP1 is up on the WiFi segment (10.6.0.0/24) and reaches its gateway, with the keepalived/VRRP master owning the virtual gateway IP at baseline
per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly states LAPTOP1 is 10.6.0.100/24, can reach its gateway (10.6.0.1) with low RTT and notes the gateway resolves to/ is owned by dswa2's VLAN40 virtual IP (keepalived/VRRP master).

The agent's observations in the log directly support the majority of the final claims (gateway and hosts reachable, VIP present on dswa2, VLANs and ports configured correctly, DNS refusing queries and ICMP redirects observed). The conclusions follow logically from those measurements and the investigation covered the necessary components to rule out a real network fault for LAPTOP1.
